headline: Strong wind and heavy rain tonight into Sunday morning, with more wet systems expected through next week.
summary: A strong cold front is crossing western Washington tonight with widespread rain and gusty south winds, peaking overnight into early Sunday. Coastal gusts had already reached 69 mph at Hoquiam Bowerman, and there is a 50 to 70 percent chance of gusts over 55 mph on the coast. Interior lowlands, including Seattle, are under a Wind Advisory, and many trees still have leaves, so power outages are possible. Waves of 22 to 28 feet are forecast along the beaches under a High Surf Warning. Thunderstorms are possible but less likely, at 20 to 30 percent on the coast and 10 to 20 percent inland. On Sunday, rain turns to showers, mostly over the North Cascades and Olympics, and the snow level drops to about 4,500 feet, so higher mountains may see some snow. Sunday evening brings a brief break before another wet, breezy system Monday, again aimed mostly at the Olympics. Wet, breezy weather continues Tuesday into Wednesday with milder temperatures, and more systems are expected late in the week. Forecasters are much less certain about next week's details, calling model guidance shaky on timing and strength. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will saturate soils and could become a concern by late next week.
changes: The thunderstorm chances first appeared in the afternoon discussion, and the coastal wind forecast was reframed from gusts as high as 60 mph to a 50 to 70 percent chance of gusts over 55 mph. The evening update added the observed 69 mph gust at Hoquiam Bowerman and noted that the lightning already detected over the ocean suggests unstable air behind the front.
